newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shenzhen H1 container handling up 122 pct.
newsitem.headline: China's Shenzhen H1 container handling up 122 pct.

text.p: Ports in the southern Chinese boomtown of Shenzhen handled a total of 471,300 containers in the first half of 1997, a year-on-year increase of 122.1 percent, the Shenzhen Special Zone Daily said on Thursday.
The newspaper attributed the rise to new international shipping lines and increased foreign trade in the city, which borders the world's busiest port of Hong Kong.

China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd, one of Shenzhen's main port facilities operators, handled 40 percent more containers between January and April 1997 than in the same 1996 period, it said.
The volume handled by Shenzhen-based Yantian International Co jumped 134 percent in the first four months of 1997, the newspaper said, without giving further detail.

Yantian International is a HK$3-billion marine container handling venture between Hutchison Whampoa, which has a 73 percent stake, and Shenzhen's Yantian Harbour Group, which holds the remaining 27 percent.
